stem.text: The height H of the water in a tank, in centimeters, connected to a reservoir whose water stands at 25 centimeters moves toward the reservoir height at a rate proportional to the difference between the reservoir height and H. At time \( t = 0 \) minutes, \( H = 5 \). Using k for the positive constant of proportionality, write a differential equation for H as a function of t and state the initial condition.

worked_solution.text: The dependent variable is H and the independent variable is t in minutes, so the rate is \( \frac{dH}{dt} \).

Proportional to the difference means a constant multiple of it. With k positive, \( k(25 - H) \) is positive when H is below 25 and negative when it is above, so H moves up toward 25 from its starting value.
The equation is \( \frac{dH}{dt} = k\left(25 - H\right) \), and the initial condition, stated separately, is \( H(0) = 5 \).

options.label: \( \frac{dH}{dt} = 25 - H \), with \( H(0) = 5 \)
options.derivation: proportional read as equal, so the constant k never appears

options.label: \( \frac{dH}{dt} = k\left(25 - 5\right) \), with \( H(0) = 5 \)
options.derivation: the initial value 5 substituted for H inside the equation, so the rate becomes a constant

options.label: \( \frac{dH}{dt} = k\left(H - 25\right) \), with \( H(0) = 5 \)
options.derivation: the difference written as H minus the level, which with k positive drives H away from 25
